submission.natural_language_explanation: L12/H2 is a retrospective 'joint readout' head: it is near-silent on open-class words themselves (mean strength 0.054 ADJ, 0.073 PROPN, 0.090 NOUN, 0.103 VERB, and 0.056 on code identifiers, 0.086 on numbers, against 0.354 on punctuation and 0.282 on coordinating conjunctions) and fires at a grammatical joint - the punctuation, coordinator, auxiliary, pronoun, subordinator, bracket or code whitespace that closes a stretch of text - where it attends back (median 1-4 tokens, but more than 8 in a quarter of the strong cases) to the lexical item that joint closes and copies that item's OV value into the joint, so the size of its write is the size of the value it copied. It therefore peaks where the closed item is a rare piece or a name ('Ref<A>' 0.82 above floor vs 'Ref<String>' 0.38, 'ESQ.', 'itis,', '%' after digits, the space before the '}' ending the function whose name it read earlier) and at ordinary prose sentence ends ('... the school is far.' 1.76, 0.47 of max), while it is predicted inactive on the open-class token itself, inside identifiers and numbers, at joints that only follow a function word or a common numeral (list comma after 'two'/'seven' 0.0-0.3 vs after 'pears' 0.61), and on prose commas after common whole words (0.1-0.6, below the 0.25 line); about 1% of scan tokens are active, and its leftovers are the ~1-in-4 cases where the peak sits on a plain content word (' people', ' started') because the copy fired at a content-word position.

rival_explanations: Broader reading: the head fires on the closed-class token class itself - any comma, full stop, coordinator or auxiliary - with the preceding word irrelevant, so a list comma after a common numeral or an ordinary prose full stop should fire as strongly as a joint that closes a rare piece or a name.

Narrower reading: it is a closing-delimiter head that reacts only to the close of a quoted, bracketed or numeric literal ('>' , '"', ')', '%', CJK closing quotes) and prose joints are incidental, so a sentence that merely ends in a full stop after a common word should stay inactive.

Lookahead reading: its write at a joint prepares the token that comes next (the new list item, the next clause subject), so its magnitude should follow the predictability of the following token rather than the identity of the preceding one; the evidence against this is that it attends back to 'questions' at -1 rather than to 'developed' at +4, and ablating it moves next-token logits by KL <= 0.16.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Detective Okonkwo, who joined the precinct in spring, solved the cipher before dawn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The sentence ends after the common noun dawn, the hypothesis's ordinary prose sentence-end peak, while the name before the comma is split into common token pieces (' Ok','on','k','wo'), so the comma itself is not the rare-name joint the words suggest and the delimiter-only rival still denies the prose full stop.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Output from the reactor rose 47% after the retrofit
adversarial_test_results.detail: A percent sign after digits is the hypothesis's own claimed rare-piece joint, its token follows the digit '7', and no comma, full stop, coordinator or auxiliary is present, so the broader closed-class-token rival should stay silent here.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The trail through the cedar grove felt long.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An ordinary prose sentence end after a common adjective is the hypothesis's stated active case ('... the school is far.'), which the delimiter-only rival denies for a prose full stop.

The whitespace token before the closing brace ends the function whose rare name was read earlier, the hypothesis's code-whitespace case in C rather than the scan's JavaScript, while the closing parenthesis gives the delimiter-only rival a separate bracket trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El cartógrafo Nuño, llegado de Cádiz, dibujó la costa entera.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The comma closes the name Nuño, whose final token 'ño' is a rare piece the hypothesis can copy, and the sentence-final full stop after entera is a second predicted prose joint that the delimiter-only rival denies.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guest list named Professor Ilse Vogt and her two assistants.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The coordinator ' and' closes the name Vogt, whose rarer piece ' Vog' sits two tokens back within the hypothesis's median attention range, and the sentence-final full stop after a common noun is a second predicted prose joint.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dirigible is moored beyond the eastern hangar.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The auxiliary ' is' closes the rare subject dirigible, whose rarer piece ' dirig' sits two tokens back within the hypothesis's median attention range, and the sentence-final full stop is a second predicted prose joint that the delimiter-only rival ignores.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The superalloy that the metallurgists forged resisted salt spray.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The relative pronoun ' that' closes the technical noun superalloy, and the sentence-final full stop after a common noun is the hypothesis's ordinary sentence-end peak, which the delimiter-only rival denies.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The specimen (collected near Mount Erebus) arrived frozen.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The closing bracket follows the proper name Erebus, and the sentence-final full stop after a common adjective is the hypothesis's ordinary sentence-end peak; the delimiter-only rival takes the bracket but not the prose full stop.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The pathology report confirmed aspergillosis, and the ward was sealed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The sentence-final full stop after a common verb is the hypothesis's ordinary prose sentence-end peak, while the comma's preceding token 'is' is a common piece of the split rare term rather than a rare piece itself, and the delimiter-only rival denies the prose full stop.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The order arrived in three, four, five, and six separate boxes for the shop
adversarial_test_results.detail: List commas after common numerals and a coordinator after a common numeral are the hypothesis's explicit inactive joints, and the sentence ends on an open-class noun with no full stop for the claimed sentence-end peak, while the broader rival still fires on every comma.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We searched under, around, and behind the old shed
adversarial_test_results.detail: Commas after prepositions are joints that only follow function words, which the hypothesis predicts inactive while the broader rival fires on any comma.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We will finish the remaining work for them before the deadline
adversarial_test_results.detail: The auxiliary follows the pronoun We, a function word, so the hypothesis predicts no copy peak even though the broader rival treats any auxiliary as active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They packed everything, then locked the door before leaving it there
adversarial_test_results.detail: The comma follows the pronoun everything, a function-word joint the hypothesis says stays inactive but the broader rival fires on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That report covered the harbour expansion in considerable detail last year
adversarial_test_results.detail: A determiner introducing a noun is not a grammatical joint at all, and every other token is an open-class word the hypothesis calls near-silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: So that everyone in the back could hear, she spoke up
adversarial_test_results.detail: The subordinator ' that' follows the function word So and the comma follows the common verb hear, both inactive by the hypothesis, while the broader rival fires on the comma.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The serial numbers 4471 8823 9014 6620 appear on the crate
adversarial_test_results.detail: Numbers themselves are near-silent in the hypothesis and the space tokens between them are not grammatical joints, so no token after the first should peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The code computes a % b without any rounding at all
adversarial_test_results.detail: The percent sign appears as a modulo operator after the determiner a, not after digits, so it is a joint following a function word that the hypothesis predicts inactive and neither delimiter rival should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Delegates signed the treaty in 1919, 1920, and 1921 beside the river
adversarial_test_results.detail: The commas follow digit tokens of common years, the hypothesis's explicit common-numeral case, though the broader rival fires on every comma and coordinator.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: La caja contenía tres, cuatro, cinco, y seis frascos para la tienda
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish list commas after common numerals and a coordinator after a common numeral reproduce the hypothesis's explicit inactive numeral joints in another language, with no sentence-final full stop to trigger the claimed sentence-end peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Después de la tormenta, los aldeanos repararon el tejado de la granja
adversarial_test_results.detail: A comma after the common noun tormenta is the prose comma the hypothesis puts below its active line, in a Spanish sentence with no final full stop, while the broader rival fires on the comma.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Camel-case code identifiers and their pieces are code tokens the hypothesis says are near-silent, and there is no comma, full stop, coordinator, auxiliary or closing literal for the rivals.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Version 2.7.14 shipped last week without any changelog whatsoever
adversarial_test_results.detail: The full-stop tokens sit after the digits 2 and 7 inside a version number, which the hypothesis says is inactive inside numbers, and removing the coordinator leaves no joint after a content word; the broader rival still reads any full stop as a joint.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the storm, the villagers repaired the roof before nightfall
adversarial_test_results.detail: A comma after a common noun in an introductory phrase is the prose comma the hypothesis puts below its active line, while the broader rival fires on it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That long run beside the canal exhausted the visiting students
adversarial_test_results.detail: The noun run is an open-class word in a sentence with no grammatical joint, so the hypothesis predicts silence regardless of its nominal part of speech.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The athletes run beside the canal every single morning without stopping
adversarial_test_results.detail: The verb run is likewise an open-class word with no following joint, so the hypothesis predicts silence on the verb itself.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: if ready return total with the pending offset from the buffer
adversarial_test_results.detail: A return keyword fragment has no comma, full stop, coordinator or auxiliary joint, and ' with' is a preposition the hypothesis does not name as a joint, so no token after the first should peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: const note = 'return total later for the operator'
adversarial_test_results.detail: A quoted string of common words closes with a quote, which the delimiter-only rival treats as its trigger but which copies only a low-value common word under the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: // return total then the helper function stops immediately
adversarial_test_results.detail: A code comment contains only ordinary words and no joint, so the hypothesis predicts no peak when the same return token sits in a comment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ledger listed seven, Zyzzyva
adversarial_test_results.detail: The comma follows the common numeral seven, the hypothesis's explicit 0.0-0.3 inactive list-comma case, while the next token is a wildly unpredictable name, so the lookahead rival should fire.
